title: Idempotency cache eviction is O(n log n) per call at cap; no concurrent eviction safety
description: When _idempotencyCache.Count > 10,000, StoreIdempotent runs (a) a full foreach over all entries checking CreatedAt against cutoff, and (b) if still over cap, _idempotencyCache.OrderBy(kv => kv.Value.CreatedAt).FirstOrDefault() — that's an O(n log n) sort over 10k entries on the hot write path. Worse, this runs under the per-KEY semaphore but NOT a global eviction lock, so N concurrent writes to N different keys at-or-above the cap each independently sort the dictionary, each independently TryRemove the oldest entry, and the eviction becomes a thundering herd. Under sustained load right at cap this burns CPU and may evict more than intended (every concurrent writer drops a different 'oldest' candidate). The TTL pre-pass mitigates by typically dropping many entries at once, but a workload of unique keys all within the 24h window hits the OrderBy path repeatedly.
recommendation: Replace the OrderBy/TryRemove pattern with a bounded-FIFO structure: either (a) track insertion order in a ConcurrentQueue<string> of keys and evict head-batch when over cap, or (b) batch-evict (drop oldest 10% in one pass under a dedicated eviction lock so concurrent calls collapse to one). At minimum, gate the eviction block with `if (Interlocked.CompareExchange(ref _evicting, 1, 0) == 0) { try {...} finally { Volatile.Write(ref _evicting, 0); } }` so only one writer sorts at a time. Also consider that batch-evicting in chunks (say 100 oldest) means a write at the cap pays the sort cost once per 100 writes instead of every write.
rationale: P14-013 added the cap; P14-064 confirmed it; neither finding considered eviction concurrency. For a long-running server that's the steady-state hot path once 10k unique idempotency keys accumulate (~3-4 days of moderate write traffic). The OrderBy pattern is exactly the kind of 'works in tests, dies under load' regression that an audit focused on test correctness wouldn't catch.

verdict.reasoning:
Verified by reading LacerteSessionManager.cs:1311-1395 and audit-findings.json. The code is exactly as described: StoreIdempotent (1364-1396) runs an O(n) foreach over the whole cache to drop expired entries, then if still over cap runs `_idempotencyCache.OrderBy(kv => kv.Value.CreatedAt)` — a full O(n log n) sort of ~10k entries on the hot write path. The eviction block runs INSIDE ExecuteWithIdempotencyLock (1317-1334), which is a PER-KEY SemaphoreSlim — concurrent writes to N different keys are NOT mutually excluded from each other's eviction passes, so the thundering-herd concern is real. The per-key semaphore design is documented at lines 1311-1316 ("per-key SemaphoreSlim") confirming there is no global eviction lock.

Phase-14 prior work: P14-013 (id at line 285 of audit-findings.json) introduced the cap with the exact OrderBy pattern in its refinedRecommendation ("scan and TryRemove all entries older than the TTL, and if still over cap, remove the oldest N by CreatedAt"). P14-064 (line 1407) confirmed it. Neither task addressed (a) eviction concurrency under per-key locking, nor (b) the O(n log n) per-call sort cost, nor (c) batch eviction to amortize. The current code comment at line 1372 even reads "Single LINQ scan over ~10k entries is fine for the cold path" — but the cold-path assumption breaks the moment the cache stabilizes at cap (then EVERY write hits the eviction block, not just an occasional one).

Severity calibration: For a single-operator stdio MCP (per CLAUDE.md "Personal tool"), concurrent same-millisecond writes from the LLM client are rare, and reaching 10k unique keys takes days. So this is hardening, not a live bug. But the fix is small, fully sim-actionable off-Windows, and prevents a real "works in tests, dies under load" regression. Severity medium (matches the finder).

Implementation cost is low: batch-evict 10% (1000 entries) per OrderBy pass amortizes the sort cost over 1000 writes, AND gating with `Interlocked.CompareExchange(ref _evicting, 1, 0)` collapses concurrent evictors to one. Two sim-only xUnit tests cover it: (a) stuff 11k entries, assert count drops to ~9k after one over-cap write, (b) fire N=50 concurrent over-cap writes with unique keys, assert final count is bounded (no over-eviction).

title: EditionDetection cached as 'Unavailable' forever on first transient probe failure
description: P14-061 made the edition probe cache-once-on-failure to honor the docstring contract 'never re-probed for the lifetime of the process'. The implementation sets _edition = EditionInfo('Unavailable', 'Unavailable', 'Unavailable') on ANY exception (BridgeUnavailable, transient COMException, RPC_SERVER_UNAVAILABLE, etc.) and never tries again. For a long-running server this means: (1) if the first SessionStatus() call happens during a brief Lacerte service hiccup or COM apartment startup race, the edition shows 'Unavailable' for the rest of the process life even after Lacerte recovers, (2) re-running Register() to refresh the 24h auth ticket does not refresh the edition cache, (3) if an operator updates Lacerte mid-session and re-registers, the cached value remains stale, and (4) AutoReconnect's retry logic is bypassed because Probe is called synchronously without retry wrapping.
recommendation: Distinguish permanent-unavailable (BridgeUnavailable with reason 'Live edition probe not yet implemented' — that's a Phase-9 code gap that won't change without a deployment) from transient-unavailable (COMException with a known transient HRESULT). Cache permanent failures forever; for transient failures, cache for a TTL (say 5 minutes) and retry on the next SessionStatus call. Alternatively, clear _edition in Register() so any successful re-registration re-probes the edition triple. Wrap the actual Probe() call with AutoReconnect.WithRetrySync so transient COM hiccups don't poison the cache.
rationale: P14-061 was added to fix a real bug (the cache was missing the throw path), but the fix overcorrected: 'cache the attempt forever' is wrong for transient errors. SessionStatus is one of the primary operator-facing diagnostic tools; baking 'Unavailable' into it for the full process lifetime over a 5ms RPC blip is a poor lifecycle behavior.

verdict.reasoning: Verified by reading LacerteSessionManager.cs lines 311-349, EditionDetection.cs, Register() lines 186-256, and the Phase-14 task list. P14-061's fix indeed catches ALL exceptions (line 331-346) and bakes the "Unavailable" sentinel into _edition for the process lifetime with no distinction between (a) permanent unavailability (the current Phase-9 stub that always throws BridgeUnavailable with "Live edition probe not yet implemented") and (b) transient COM/RPC failures that will appear once Phase 9 wires the real probe. Confirmed via Grep that Register() never clears _edition — so a re-register after the 24h auth window (or after an operator restarts the Lacerte service mid-session) does NOT refresh the edition triple. Confirmed Probe is called directly without AutoReconnect.WithRetrySync wrapping (Register() IS wrapped at line 223, but the edition path is not). The cached-Unavailable behavior in SessionStatus is then silently surfaced because SessionStatus's outer catch at line 280 also coerces edition probe failures to null — but with P14-061 the inner Unavailable triple is returned directly, so SessionStatus surfaces stale "Unavailable" even after Lacerte recovers. P14-061 and P14-056 are the only Phase-14 tasks touching this code; neither distinguishes transient vs permanent nor invalidates on Register(). The current symptom is latent today (sim Probe never throws; live Probe is always permanent until Phase 9), but the finding is correct that the fix overshoots and will hurt the moment Phase 9 wires real late-bound COM reads. Medium severity is fair — operator-facing diagnostic (lacerte_session_status) is the only consumer. The simplest valuable fix today is to clear _edition in Register() so a re-register naturally refreshes the cache; the transient-vs-permanent TTL split is a Phase-9-or-later concern and would be premature now.
verdict.refinedRecommendation:
Two minimal sim-testable fixes; defer the TTL/transient classification to Phase 9 when real COMExceptions can actually be thrown.

(1) Clear the edition cache in Register() — add `lock (_editionLock) { _edition = null; }` at the top of Register() (before the WireLog wrapper). This means any successful re-registration (24h auth refresh, mid-session Lacerte restart, operator-triggered re-register after a service hiccup) naturally re-probes the edition. Document the invariant in the _edition field comment: "Cleared on Register() so re-auth refreshes the triple; otherwise one-shot per registration."

(2) Add a unit test in LacerteSessionManagerTests.cs using a fake ILacerteBridge that records Probe-equivalent call count: (a) bridge throws on first Probe → SessionStatus returns Unavailable triple, (b) call Register() (which succeeds), (c) bridge configured to succeed on next Probe → second SessionStatus returns the real triple. Asserts Probe was invoked exactly twice across the two SessionStatus calls. Today this can be smoke-tested by having the test inject a bridge via the internal test ctor.

Explicitly NOT in scope right now: (a) wrapping Probe in AutoReconnect.WithRetrySync — Phase 9 should do this when it wires the real late-bound reads, not in advance against a stub that only throws BridgeUnavailable; (b) transient-vs-permanent HRESULT classification — same reasoning, premature without a real COM call to classify against. File a Phase-9 follow-up note in DECISIONS.md so this isn't lost: "When EditionDetection.Probe gains real COM reads (Phase 9), wrap in AutoReconnect.WithRetrySync and distinguish RPC_SERVER_UNAVAILABLE (transient, TTL-cache) from BridgeUnavailable (permanent, lifetime-cache)."

title: No proactive 24h-auth-expiry probe; operator gets raw NotSignedIn instead of 9100 SessionExpired
description: The session manager knows ExpiresAt (set on Register at line 230/246) and SessionStatus correctly computes MinutesUntilExpiry. SyntheticStatusCodes 9100 'SessionExpired' is defined with a friendly remediation message ('Run lacerte_register to re-authenticate'). But NO write/read chokepoint checks `DateTimeOffset.UtcNow > ExpiresAt` before dispatching the wire call. The flow today is reactive: a tool call after 24h hits the bridge, the SDK returns TAPIStatus NotSignedIn (203), the operator sees a raw integer status. The synthetic 9100 with its operator-friendly message is never emitted. For a long-running session the friendly synthetic code is the entire point — it tells the operator what to DO rather than handing them a TAPIStatus to decode.
recommendation: Add a private bool IsAuthExpired() helper that returns ExpiresAt.HasValue && DateTimeOffset.UtcNow >= ExpiresAt.Value, and call it inside RequireContext (or as a separate Throw-if-expired helper) at the top of every write/read chokepoint. On true, throw new LacerteSDKError(SyntheticStatusCodes.SessionExpired, ctx) — proactive 9100 instead of reactive 203. The check is essentially free (one DateTimeOffset comparison) and turns the cliff-edge 24h failure into a clean structured error with the documented remediation.
rationale: The 9100 code, the +24h ExpiresAt stamp, and the SessionStatus MinutesUntilExpiry computation all exist and are consistent with the operator-facing UX in agent 02 §6 — but nothing wires them together. The audit-findings.json shows no Phase-14 task addressed the proactive expiry probe. The reviewer asked specifically: 'when SetContext is called after expiry, does the response give a clear remediation? Is there a probe before each call or only reactive?' The current answer is 'reactive only.'

verdict.reasoning:
Verified directly. Real issue: LacerteSessionManager.ExpiresAt is set on Register (lines 230/246) and read by SessionStatus (lines 265-268) for the MinutesUntilExpiry display, but NOTHING in the chokepoints consults it. RequireContext (line 980-988) only null-checks Context — no expiry probe. AutoReconnect.cs:137 explicitly comments that NotSignedIn propagates unchanged ("need re-auth, not retry"). In sim, SimulationStore has an _sessionExpired latch but it's env-var-toggled (LACERTE_SIM_EXPIRED=1), NOT wall-clock driven, so a sim session left running past +24h would never trigger any expired check either. Both modes are reactive-only.

One factual inaccuracy in the finding: it references SyntheticStatusCodes.SessionExpired at code 9100 — that constant does not exist. The actual auth-lifecycle codes are LoginExpired=9007 (validation range, with the operator-friendly StatusInfo message "Run lacerte_register to re-authenticate (consent is one-time; only the sign-in needs refresh).") and ReAuthRequired=9101 (in the 9100 auth-lifecycle range). 9100 itself is unused. The underlying defect — no proactive probe, operator gets raw 203 instead of a friendly synthetic code — is fully valid, but the recommendation must use the right constant.

NOT a Phase-14 duplicate: searched audit-findings.json for SessionExpired/9100/IsAuthExpired/proactive-expir/expiry-probe/24h-auth (case insensitive) and Todo.md Phase 14 — the only related Phase-14 work is P14-013 (idempotency cache TTL, different concern) and a README troubleshooting entry that *mentions* the 24h expiry symptom but does not add a code-level probe. The Sim's existing _sessionExpired latch is env-only and confirms nothing was wired to clock time.

Fully actionable off-Windows: pure in-process check on a DateTimeOffset comparison, no Lacerte SDK, no Windows. Test seam: the existing test-only ctor (line 166) can be used; need a small additional hook to inject a fake clock OR an internal setter for ExpiresAt so a test can pre-stamp it in the past. Both are one-line additions.

Useful: in a 24h+ session every subsequent write-tool call returns an opaque integer (203 in live, or in sim today: nothing at all because the wall-clock check doesn't exist) with no remediation hint. The 9007 synthetic code's documented Remediation field ("Run lacerte_register to re-authenticate") is the entire DX point. Fix is ~15 lines + a focused test. Not bikeshedding.

title: Sim-mode tools never gate on IsRegistered — observational divergence from live
description: RequireContext() throws ContextNotSet (9006) when Context is null, but no chokepoint checks `IsRegistered`. In simulation mode you can call lacerte_field_write / lacerte_detail_write / lacerte_table_read without ever having called Register — all the gates pass, the sim store accepts the write, and the response says success. In live mode the bridge would reject with NotSignedIn (3) because the COM Register call is a hard prerequisite. The two-mode discipline rule in CLAUDE.md (`Simulation and live must be observationally identical for the happy path`) is violated for the most basic gate of all. CreateClient is the one path that *does* check IsRegistered (via SimulationStore.SimulateCreateClient since P14-030), but every other write/read path bypasses it.
recommendation: Add `if (!IsRegistered) throw new LacerteSDKError(StatusCodes.NotSignedIn, ...)` as the first synchronous gate after RequireContext() in WriteField, WriteDetail, and every Read* chokepoint. Sim mode honors this because Register() flips IsRegistered=true on the AccessGranted path. Add a regression test that confirms a fresh session manager rejects WriteField/ReadClient/etc with NotSignedIn before Register is called. The fix is one line per chokepoint plus a tiny test pass.
rationale: Round-1 P14-030 fixed CreateClient's sim-vs-live gate divergence but only for that one path. The same class of bug — sim skipping the IsRegistered latch — applies to every other chokepoint. This is exactly the kind of silent divergence the round-1 audit set out to eliminate, just missed across the rest of the surface.

verdict.reasoning: VERIFIED: The divergence is real and not addressed by Phase 14. Concrete read of LacerteSessionManager.cs confirms: (a) IsRegistered is a manager-side latch flipped true only on Register() AccessGranted (line 228, 244); (b) WriteField (line 645), WriteDetail (line 788), ListClients (459), ReadClient (488), ReadTableCore (519), ReadDetail (579), ReadEFStatus (600) all call only RequireContext() — none check IsRegistered. (c) The sim write helpers ApplySimFieldWrite / ApplySimDetailWrite go direct-to-ModuleStore, explicitly bypassing SimulationStore.SimulateFieldWrite per the comment at lines 1041-1047 — and SimulateFieldWrite is where the NotSignedIn-equivalent (`_sessionExpired`) gate lives (SimulationStore.cs:291). (d) Only CreateClient delegates to SimulationStore.SimulateCreateClient (post-P14-030), which performs the full IsRegistered gate at SimulationStore.cs:495-499. So the entire write+read surface except CreateClient skips the spec gate in sim. In live mode, the COM SDK itself will reject WriteField with NotSignedIn (203), so the divergence shows up as: sim returns Success, live returns NotSignedIn — exactly the kind of observational divergence CLAUDE.md "two-mode discipline" rule was written to prevent. Not a Phase-14 duplicate: P14-030 fixed only CreateClient; P14-003 covered live reads (which currently throw BridgeUnavailable, but that's a separate scaffolding issue); no Phase-14 task addresses a manager-side IsRegistered gate for WriteField/WriteDetail/Read*. Caveat on severity: read paths are currently unreachable in live mode anyway (P14-003 ThrowIfLiveUnwired), so the read divergence is latent until Phase 9 wires ODBC reads — but the write divergence (WriteField/WriteDetail) is reachable today because the live bridge IS wired for writes. The IsRegistered field also gates the AppId/Register lifecycle so adding a sim-side gate keeps the SessionStatus + idempotency cache semantics honest. Fix is one line per chokepoint plus tests — fully sim-only.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Add a single private helper `RequireRegistered()` next to `RequireContext()` (around line 980) that throws `LacerteSDKError(StatusCodes.NotSignedIn, { ["reason"] = "Register() must succeed (AccessGranted) before this operation." })` when `!IsRegistered`. Call it as the first synchronous gate after `RequireContext()` in: WriteField (line 645), WriteDetail (788), ReadClient (488), ListClients (459), ReadTableCore (519), ReadDetail (579), ReadEFStatus (600). CreateClient already passes through SimulationStore.SimulateCreateClient which has its own gate, but adding the manager-side check there too is fine for uniformity. Do NOT switch the sim write helpers to delegate to SimulationStore.SimulateFieldWrite — the existing comment at LacerteSessionManager.cs:1041-1047 explains the gate-order intentionally lives at the manager (idempotency/access-map runs first), and the SimulationStore-side `_sessionExpired` latch handles the *expired* case separately from the *never-registered* case. The new manager-side IsRegistered check covers the "never registered" case which the sim store cannot see (its `_registered` field is set by SimulationStore.Register, which IS called from LacerteSessionManager.Register at line 241 — so flipping IsRegistered=true at the manager and `_registered=1` at the sim are coupled and the gate stays consistent). Tests: (1) `WriteField_BeforeRegister_ThrowsNotSignedIn` in LacerteSessionManagerTests.cs (sim); (2) `ReadClient_BeforeRegister_ThrowsNotSignedIn`; (3) `WriteDetail_BeforeRegister_ThrowsNotSignedIn`; (4) update FullFlowTests to confirm the happy path (Register → SetContext → Read/Write) still passes; (5) add one regression confirming SessionStatus snapshot still works pre-Register (it's an in-memory status read with no wire impact, so it must NOT gate on IsRegistered). Update DECISIONS.md with a brief entry "Sim-mode chokepoints gate on IsRegistered to match live SDK's NotSignedIn rejection" cross-referencing the CLAUDE.md two-mode rule. Tighten ARCHITECTURE.md Boundary Invariant #8 (or add #11) to read "Every wire chokepoint gates on IsRegistered before any access-map / idempotency / wire work — sim and live identical."

title: Idempotency lock map (_idempotencyLocks) is genuinely unbounded; only the cache evicts
description: P14-005 added per-key SemaphoreSlim serialization via ExecuteWithIdempotencyLock, and P14-013/P14-064 added a 10k-entry + 24h-TTL eviction policy to _idempotencyCache. But the eviction logic in StoreIdempotent (lines 1374-1395) only prunes _idempotencyCache — it never touches _idempotencyLocks. Every unique idempotencyKey ever seen contributes one permanent SemaphoreSlim entry to the lock dictionary. With LacerteSessionManager being a process-lifetime singleton (per CLAUDE.md), a long-running MCP session that processes (say) 50k unique idempotent writes over a week leaves 50k SemaphoreSlims pinned in memory, all GC-rooted via the static-ish dictionary, even though _idempotencyCache itself stayed at 10k. The HANDOFF.md note "cheap to leak (one SemaphoreSlim per unique key)" assumes a short-lived session — this is an MCP stdio server that runs for the operator's full session. The P14-005 refinedRecommendation specifically suggested "or add a periodic compaction tied to session lifetime"; neither happened.
recommendation: When StoreIdempotent evicts an entry from _idempotencyCache (either expired or oldest-when-over-cap), also TryRemove the matching key from _idempotencyLocks and Dispose the semaphore. Guard against the race where another thread is currently holding the lock: only remove if `sem.CurrentCount == 1` (no one waiting AND no one holding) at the moment of eviction; otherwise let the next eviction cycle catch it. Add a test that creates 100 unique idempotency keys, forces eviction, and asserts _idempotencyLocks count is bounded.
rationale: Phase-14 audit P14-013 and P14-064 explicitly closed cache leaks, but missed the parallel lock-map leak created by P14-005. The fix is asymmetric: cache bounded, locks unbounded. Easy to fix in-session.

verdict.reasoning: Confirmed by direct read of LacerteSessionManager.cs. _idempotencyLocks (line 105-106) is a ConcurrentDictionary populated via GetOrAdd at line 1324 with no removal path anywhere except Dispose() at line 1465 (process exit). The eviction logic in StoreIdempotent (lines 1374-1395) operates only on _idempotencyCache and never touches _idempotencyLocks. This is the exact asymmetry described: cache is bounded at 10k entries with 24h TTL, locks grow forever. Grepping audit-findings.json confirms no Phase-14 task addresses lock-map eviction — P14-005 explicitly chose to leak ("cheap to leak ... or add a periodic compaction tied to session lifetime") and the compaction half was never delivered; P14-013/P14-064 only covered the cache. No existing test exercises lock-map bounds. The fix is fully sim-actionable: ~10 lines in StoreIdempotent + an xUnit test that creates 100 unique keys, triggers eviction, and asserts _idempotencyLocks.Count is bounded (needs internal-visible-to-test exposure of the field count, or a debug accessor). Severity caveat: for a single-operator MCP tool (CLAUDE.md), 50k unique keys/week is implausible; SemaphoreSlim is ~80-100 bytes + key string ~50 bytes; realistic leak is single-digit MB over months. But the asymmetry is a real code-quality defect — the cache has rigorous bounded-memory invariants that the lock map silently violates, and the fix is one block in StoreIdempotent. Worth landing as a follow-up to P14-005/013/064.

title: EFStatus sim/live divergence: SQL uses LEFT OUTER JOIN, sim uses INNER JOIN
description: P14-053 rewrote SqlTemplates.EfStatusJoin to use `left outer join [EFilings] ... left outer join [EFStatuses]` so live results include clients with no eFiling rows (with null EFId/Status). But the sim path in LacerteSessionManager.ReadEFStatus (lines 604-615) is `from f in module.EFilings join s in module.EFStatuses on f.Id equals s.EFilingId` — a LINQ INNER join that EXCLUDES clients without eFilings AND EXCLUDES eFilings without statuses. Net effect when Phase 9 wires live: sim returns N rows, live returns N+K rows (K = clients with no eFilings yet) — the exact "two-mode discipline observationally identical for the happy path" invariant the audit was closing. The audit verdict for P14-053 caught the column projection drift but not the JOIN-type drift. SqlTemplatesTests verify column names but not JOIN semantics; no parity test seeds a client without eFilings.
recommendation: Rewrite the sim's ReadEFStatus to be a LEFT OUTER JOIN (LINQ's `from f in module.EFilings join s in module.EFStatuses on f.Id equals s.EFilingId into gj from s in gj.DefaultIfEmpty() select ...`) AND to start from `module.Clients` (so clients without eFilings also appear, matching the SQL's `from ci ... left outer join ef ...` shape). When the join misses, emit nulls for EFilingId/EFId/InstanceId/Status/StatusDate. Add a parity test that seeds (a) one client with eFiling+status, (b) one client with eFiling but no status, (c) one client with no eFiling — assert all three appear in the result with the right null fields.
rationale: P14-053 fixed the column-projection half but introduced/left a JOIN-semantics divergence. The CLAUDE.md "observationally identical" invariant is exactly the thing this audit promised to enforce; the silent miss will only surface on a real Lacerte box (after Phase 9), too late to catch cheaply.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED. Direct code reading of LacerteSessionManager.cs:604-615 shows sim path is `from f in module.EFilings join s in module.EFStatuses on f.Id equals s.EFilingId` — a LINQ inner join starting from EFilings. SqlTemplates.cs:208-213 (post P14-021) is `from [DATA1-Client Info] as ci left outer join [EFilings] as ef on ci.C1_0 = ef.ClientId left outer join [EFStatuses] as s on ef.Id = s.EFilingId` — outer join starting from Clients. The two return DIFFERENT row sets when (a) a client has no EFiling, or (b) an EFiling has no status. Sim drops both; live includes both with NULLs. This is a clean violation of CLAUDE.md's "Simulation and live must be observationally identical for the happy path" invariant — exactly the rule P14-021 was meant to enforce.

DUPLICATE CHECK: P14-021 (the only EFStatus-related Phase-14 task) explicitly addressed *column projection* parity. Its verdict reasoning says "Fix is a pure string edit in a const" — the entire framing was column names. The SqlTemplatesTests P14-021 added (lines 228-235, 246-259) verify column names and join-clause presence, but never assert ROW-SET parity. No Phase-14 task touched the sim's LINQ inner join. The two parity-leg tests for ReadEFStatus run sim-against-itself (the live leg isn't wired), so a divergence cannot be caught today even with parity tests in place. The current seed always creates EFiling+EFStatus together, so even a future round-trip parity test would miss case (c) "client with no EFiling" without an explicit seed.

ACTIONABLE OFF-WINDOWS: yes — pure LINQ rewrite + seed-extension + sim-only assertion. No COM, no ODBC, no Windows.

USEFUL: yes — this is the exact silent-divergence trap the audit was meant to close; will only surface post-Phase-9 on a real Lacerte box, the most expensive place to catch it. Also fixes a latent doc/code mismatch since SqlTemplates.EfStatusJoin's xml-doc explicitly cites the parity invariant against ReadEFStatus.
verdict.refinedRecommendation:
Three-part fix, all in sim land:

1) `src/LacertMCP.Server/Session/LacerteSessionManager.cs` ReadEFStatus (604-615): rewrite to start from `module.Clients.Values` (DATA1) and outer-join EFilings then EFStatuses, so the row set matches the SQL's `from ci left outer join ef left outer join s` shape exactly. Concrete LINQ:
```
var joined = from c in module.Clients.Values
             from f in module.EFilings.Where(x => x.ClientId == (string)c.Fields["C1_0"]).DefaultIfEmpty()
             from s in module.EFStatuses.Where(x => f != null && x.EFilingId == f.Id).DefaultIfEmpty()
             select (IReadOnlyDictionary<string, object?>)new Dictionary<string, object?>
             {
                 ["ClientId"]   = c.Fields["C1_0"],
                 ["EFilingId"]  = f?.Id,            // null when client has no eFiling
                 ["EFId"]       = f?.EFId,          // null when client has no eFiling
                 ["InstanceId"] = f?.InstanceId,    // null when client has no eFiling
                 ["Status"]     = s?.Status,        // null when eFiling has no status
                 ["StatusDate"] = s?.StatusDate,    // null when eFiling has no status
             };
```
Key-name ordering should match the SQL SELECT alias order (ClientId, EFilingId, EFId, InstanceId, Status, StatusDate) so the dictionary's insertion-ordered enumeration matches what an ODBC reader would yield.

2) `src/LacertMCP.Server/Session/SimulationStore.Seed.cs` (115-128): currently `if (c.EFStatus != null)` seeds BOTH an EFiling and a Status. Extend the seed so at least one fixture client has an EFiling with no status (push an EFiling, skip the EFStatuses add) and at least one has no EFiling at all (the path already exists — any client with `EFStatus == null` qualifies, but verify at least one such Individual + Corp client is present in the canonical TY24 seed). Document the three cases inline so future contractors don't "helpfully" delete them.

3) `src/LacertMCP.Tests/Parity/RoundTripTests.cs` ReadEFStatus_ReturnsRowsWithEfilingId (141-150): split into three assertions — (a) at least one row with non-null EFilingId/Status (full join hit), (b) at least one row with non-null EFilingId but null Status (EFiling-without-Status case), (c) at least one row with the seeded "no-eFiling" client's ClientId and null EFilingId/EFId/InstanceId/Status (client-without-eFiling case). Without (b)+(c) the parity contract is unenforceable.

Do NOT touch SqlTemplates.cs — the post-P14-021 SQL is correct; the bug is sim-side only. Also: while you're in ReadEFStatus, the leading XML doc-comment still says "TY19+ EFilings JOIN EFStatuses" — update it to "DATA1 LEFT OUTER JOIN EFilings LEFT OUTER JOIN EFStatuses" to match the SQL template's docstring style and remove the "INNER JOIN" mental model.

title: Idempotency cache uses absolute expiry — silent surprise re-execution at 24h boundary
description: P14-013/P14-064 added a 24h TTL on idempotency entries 'matching the 24h Intuit auth window'. The implementation in TryReplayIdempotent uses absolute creation time (`DateTimeOffset.UtcNow - entry.CreatedAt > IdempotencyTtl`) — never refreshed on a cache hit. Symptom: an operator passes idempotencyKey='K1' for WriteField at t=0 (entry stored). At t=23.5h they pass the same key+payload (cache hit, no SDK call — correct). At t=24.1h they pass the same key+payload — the entry is evicted as expired, the write executes AGAIN against the SDK, and a successful first-execution side effect (a row already written) is now potentially DOUBLED. The user-facing contract was 'same key + same payload returns cached result' (CreateClientTools.cs:57 description); the silent eviction violates it. Worse, the 24h auth-window framing was the original justification — but auth re-registration doesn't actually invalidate the side effect of a prior write, so coupling these two TTLs is conceptually muddled.
recommendation: Two options: (a) Switch to sliding-window TTL — on cache HIT, refresh entry.CreatedAt (or store LastAccessedAt as a separate column). The semantic becomes 'same key+payload stays valid as long as you keep replaying it within 24h'. (b) Keep absolute TTL but on eviction-by-expiry, throw a NEW synthetic 9103 IdempotencyEvicted (the verdict on P14-064 actually suggested this naming) so the caller sees an explicit signal instead of a silent re-execute. Either way, add a test where a key+payload pair stored at t=0 is replayed at t=23h59m (must hit cache), then a fresh replay at t=24h01m (must throw 9103 — or hit cache if sliding). Update the audit-findings P14-013/P14-064 reasoning + DECISIONS.md to document which semantic was chosen.
rationale: Round-1 audit refined the cache to add 24h TTL but neither finding nor refined recommendation explicitly addressed sliding-window vs absolute semantics, nor surfaced the silent-re-execute risk. The 24h boundary is exactly the threshold most operators will hit in normal use (overnight pause + next-day replay), so the surprise is high-probability. Pure sim-actionable, ~10 lines + one test.

verdict.reasoning: Verified at LacerteSessionManager.cs:1336-1396. The TTL implementation is absolute (entry.CreatedAt vs UtcNow), never refreshed on hit. Tool [Description] attributes on CreateClientTools.cs:57, FieldWriteTools.cs:49, and DetailsTools.cs:97 still advertise "Same key + same payload returns the cached result" with no mention of the 24h expiry — so the contract documented to the model is now silently inaccurate post-P14-013/P14-064. The behavioral change the finder proposes (sliding-window OR new 9103 IdempotencyEvicted code) was already explicitly considered and rejected during round 1: P14-064's refined recommendation says "skip the new synthetic code... a never-stored key and an evicted-then-replayed key are observationally identical to a well-behaved caller and adding a new code for it just expands surface area." So the agent's core recommendation duplicates the rejected branch of P14-064's analysis. What is genuinely NEW: (a) the docstring/[Description] string is now stale relative to actual behavior, and (b) the chosen absolute-TTL semantic was decided but never pinned by a test, so a future refactor to sliding-window won't trip any guardrail. Severity is honestly low — single-operator stdio tool, write volumes per session are dozens not 10k, and overnight-pause-replay-next-day is a niche pattern. Confidence medium because the behavior question itself was already adjudicated; only the docs+test slice is undisputedly new.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Drop the behavioral-change ask (sliding-window OR 9103 IdempotencyEvicted) — P14-064's verdict already chose absolute TTL with silent miss-on-expiry and rejected the new synthetic code as surface-bloat. Limit the work to two doc+test patches: (1) Update the three tool [Description] strings to surface the TTL bound — change CreateClientTools.cs:57, FieldWriteTools.cs:49, DetailsTools.cs:97 from "Same key + same payload returns the cached result" to "Same key + same payload returns the cached result for up to 24h after the first call; replays after that re-execute (treated as a new key)." (2) Pin the chosen absolute semantic with one xUnit test in LacertMCP.Tests/Session/LacerteSessionManagerTests.cs using a test-only seam — either an internal `internal void SetIdempotencyEntryCreatedAtForTest(string key, DateTimeOffset)` exposed via InternalsVisibleTo, or reflection on `_idempotencyCache` to backdate CreatedAt on a stored entry. Two facts: (a) entry backdated to 23h59m ago → replay returns the cached result; (b) entry backdated to 24h01m ago → replay re-executes (observable via the same signal WriteParityTests uses: row count grows by 1 again, or a counter on a test bridge). Add one short DECISIONS.md entry titled "Idempotency cache TTL is absolute, not sliding" recording the round-1 decision and pointing at the tool [Description] strings + test as the pinning artifacts. Single PR, ~30 lines net, no behavior change. Skip the muddled-coupling critique in the original — the 24h-matches-auth-window framing is a reasonable mnemonic even if the two TTLs aren't causally linked, and rewriting it has no functional benefit.

title: No tests for idempotency cache TTL + size-cap eviction
description: Phase-14 tasks P14-013 / P14-064 added cache size cap (IdempotencyCacheMaxEntries) and TTL eviction (IdempotencyTtl) at LacerteSessionManager.cs:1336+. The TryReplayIdempotent path explicitly evicts on expiry and StoreIdempotent does opportunistic over-cap eviction by oldest CreatedAt. A grep for 'IdempotencyCacheMaxEntries|IdempotencyTtl|cache.*evict' across LacertMCP.Tests returns zero matches. The 'expired entry treated as miss' branch and the 'over cap drops oldest' branch are untested; a regression that flips the inequality (>= vs >) or skips the cleanup pass would not be caught.
recommendation: Add a test that exposes IdempotencyCacheMaxEntries via reflection / internal const, fills cache to N+1 entries, and asserts only N entries remain after the last StoreIdempotent call. Add a second test using a manipulated DateTimeOffset (or a test-only IClock seam) that asserts an expired key triggers a re-execute rather than returning the stale cached result. The TTL test is non-trivial without a clock seam — at minimum add an internal helper to force-expire an entry for tests.
rationale: Cache eviction logic is exactly the class of code where off-by-one bugs (>= cap vs > cap) and timing assumptions silently corrupt state. Zero coverage is unusual for a Phase-14 lens-9 (perf) hardening.

verdict.reasoning: Verified directly. P14-013 + P14-064 shipped the eviction code at LacerteSessionManager.cs:1336-1395 (TryReplayIdempotent expires via `> IdempotencyTtl`, StoreIdempotent over-caps via `> IdempotencyCacheMaxEntries` with expired-first then oldest-by-CreatedAt prune). The Phase-14 refined recommendation for P14-013 EXPLICITLY listed the three tests as required deliverables ("(a) expired entry on TryReplay returns miss + re-executes, (b) over-cap StoreIdempotent prunes oldest entries, (c) replay-with-same-payload within TTL still hits"), but only (c) actually shipped — confirmed by Grep across LacertMCP.Tests for `expir|evict|MaxEntries|TTL|CreatedAt` returning zero matches in any idempotency test. The two existing idempotency tests in LacerteSessionManagerTests.cs:262-310 cover only the hit-same-payload short-circuit and the conflict-on-different-payload throw. The eviction code has subtle inequality boundaries (strict `>`) where an off-by-one flip would silently break the contract and not fail any test. Actionable off-Windows: pure in-process data-structure logic, InternalsVisibleTo("LacertMCP.Tests") is already wired in AssemblyAttributes.cs:11 so reflection can reach `_idempotencyCache` and the private const/static-readonly fields. Useful: this is a known-risky code class (cache eviction with caller-supplied keys) on a hardening lens that the Phase-14 reviewer themselves flagged as test-required. Not a duplicate — P14-013 closed the implementation but its own refinedRecommendation's test asks are unfulfilled.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Add three xUnit tests to src/LacertMCP.Tests/Session/LacerteSessionManagerTests.cs in the existing "Idempotency cache state machine" region. Use reflection (InternalsVisibleTo is already configured) on the private `_idempotencyCache` ConcurrentDictionary<string, IdempotencyCacheEntry> field. (1) `WriteDetail_IdempotencyKey_ExpiredEntry_ReExecutes`: do a first WriteDetail with idempotencyKey "exp1"; reflect into _idempotencyCache, retrieve the entry, and replace it with `new IdempotencyCacheEntry(entry.PayloadFingerprint, entry.Result, DateTimeOffset.UtcNow.AddHours(-25))` (older than the 24h TTL); record the detail count, call WriteDetail again with the same key+payload, and assert the count INCREASED by 1 (re-executed, not replayed). (3) `StoreIdempotent_OverCap_PrunesExpiredFirst`: seed `IdempotencyCacheMaxEntries` entries where half have CreatedAt > 24h ago and half are fresh; trigger one write; assert all expired entries are gone AND no fresh entry was evicted. As a follow-on tiny refactor (optional, only if reflection is judged too brittle), bump `IdempotencyCacheMaxEntries` from `private const` to `internal const` and add an `internal void ForceExpireForTests(string key)` helper that rewrites the entry's CreatedAt to UtcNow - IdempotencyTtl - 1s — cleaner than reflection and signals test-supported surface. title: _newApisCache and _edition not cleared on Register() — re-auth doesn't refresh per-process derivatives
description: Register() updates IsRegistered/RegisteredAt/ExpiresAt on success but does NOT clear _newApisCache or _edition. After a long-running session the operator re-runs Register() (because the 24h ticket expired and they want a fresh session) — but if a prior CanUseNewApis probe failed transiently and got cached (via the AutoReconnect.WithRetrySync wrapping in CanUseNewApis at line 432-435, which still propagates final-failure exceptions through GetOrAdd — actually GetOrAdd's factory exception does NOT cache, so transient probe failures DON'T pollute _newApisCache; this is the saving grace), then for _edition specifically (cached on first failure as 'Unavailable' per P14-061) the re-Register does nothing to refresh it. Compound with finding 'EditionDetection cached as Unavailable forever': re-registering after a Lacerte version bump shows the wrong (or 'Unavailable') edition until process restart.
recommendation: In Register() on the AccessGranted branch, clear the derived caches: `_edition = null;` (with _editionLock held). Optionally clear _newApisCache too — the (year, module) → useNewApis answer is technically stable across re-auth so this is defensive, but free. Document the contract: 'A successful Register() invalidates EditionInfo so the next SessionStatus re-probes.'
rationale: Pair fix with the EditionDetection issue above. Without clearing on re-auth, the operator's only path to refresh the edition is process restart, which defeats the purpose of having Register() as a re-auth surface. Low severity because today's wire-disconnect cache pollution is only the edition string, not anything functional — but lifecycle correctness matters for the documented re-auth workflow.

verdict.reasoning:
Verified by reading LacerteSessionManager.cs lines 85-94 (field declarations), 186-256 (Register), and 311-349 (EnsureEditionProbed). Both caches are confirmed:

(1) _newApisCache is a ConcurrentDictionary<(int,char), bool> populated via GetOrAdd at line 418-438. The finding's claim that GetOrAdd does NOT cache factory exceptions is correct — Microsoft documents that an exception in the valueFactory propagates and the key is NOT added — so transient CanUseNewApis probe failures do NOT poison the cache. Successful answers persist for process lifetime.

(2) _edition is a single nullable field. EnsureEditionProbed (P14-061) explicitly caches the 'Unavailable' sentinel on probe failure (line 345) so the docstring's 'never re-probed for the lifetime of the process' contract holds.

(3) Register() AccessGranted branch (lines 226-231 live, 242-247 sim) updates only IsRegistered/RegisteredAt/ExpiresAt. Neither _edition nor _newApisCache is touched.

(4) Cross-checked Phase-14 task list (P14-001..P14-071 in Todo.md): P14-061 added the cache-failure-as-sentinel behavior but did NOT add cache invalidation on Register(). The audit-findings.json EnsureEditionProbed entry's refinedRecommendation explicitly stops at 'cache the failure'; it never mentions clearing on re-auth. This finding is genuinely new and is the natural follow-on to P14-061.

(5) Real-world impact is low — the dominant operator workflow is start → use → stop, and a fresh process re-probes from scratch. The 24h Intuit auth window plus stdio MCP lifetime mean mid-process Register() is rare. But the CLI does expose `lacerte-mcp register` as a re-auth surface, and after P14-061 the edition string can semantically lie until process restart, which contradicts the documented intent of having Register() as a refresh point. Fix is ~6 lines + a sim-only unit test using the test ctor with a throwing fake bridge that flips to non-throwing on second probe.

(6) The finding's own analysis of _newApisCache being a defensive (not strictly necessary) clear is correct — the (year, module) → useNewApis answer is a property of the Lacerte install, not the auth ticket, so it's stable across re-auth. Clearing it is cheap insurance for the case where a future Lacerte upgrade changes TY21+ support mid-process.
verdict.refinedRecommendation:
In LacerteSessionManager.Register() on AccessGranted (both sim path line 247 and live path line 231), invalidate the derived per-process caches so a successful re-auth refreshes them:

```csharp
// After setting IsRegistered/RegisteredAt/ExpiresAt on AccessGranted:
lock (_editionLock) { _edition = null; }
_newApisCache.Clear();
```

Rationale per cache:
- _edition: REQUIRED after P14-061. Without it, a transient first-probe failure (e.g. live bridge BridgeUnavailable during a pre-Phase-9 startup, or a slow COM probe timing out once) sticks 'Unavailable/Unavailable/Unavailable' to the snapshot for process lifetime — the operator's documented escape hatch (`lacerte-mcp register` re-auth) does not refresh it, only process restart does. That defeats the point of Register() being a re-auth surface.
- _newApisCache: DEFENSIVE / cheap insurance. The (year, module) → bool answer is a property of the installed Lacerte build, not the auth ticket, so it survives re-auth correctly today. Clearing it costs ~9 entries max (1 per module) and protects against a future Lacerte version-bump mid-process; not strictly required.

Add one sim-only xUnit test in LacerteSessionManagerTests using the internal test ctor with an ILacerteBridge fake whose first probe throws and second succeeds: assert SessionStatus().Edition returns 'Unavailable' before Register(), then after a second Register() call returns the success triple. Document the contract in the Register() XML doc: 'A successful Register() invalidates the cached EditionInfo and CanUseNewApis answers so the next SessionStatus()/CanUseNewApis() re-probes the bridge.' Add a one-line cross-reference comment at the _edition declaration site (line 93) pointing to Register() so a future contributor doesn't re-introduce the leak.

Do NOT clear IsRegistered/RegisteredAt/ExpiresAt or Context — Register() already manages those; only the derived probe caches need clearing on success. Do NOT touch the failure branches (lines 234-237, 251-253) — those already leave IsRegistered=false and a failed re-register correctly does not invalidate the prior successful probe state.

title: Read paths log args but not result-shape — no result-size telemetry
description: Read chokepoints (`ListClients`, `ReadTable`, `ReadEFStatus`, `ReadSubclients`, `ReadStates`, `ReadStatuses`, `ReadForms`, `ReadDetail`) wrap their bodies in `WireLog.Record` — but the `result` field in the log line is the FULL payload, then post-redacted. For `ReadTable(1)` against a 5000-client DBF this writes 5000 row dicts to disk per call (~2 MB per log line). Two issues: (1) the log balloons (contributes to finding #2), and (2) the operator looking at logs cannot quickly see "this call returned 5000 rows in 800ms" without parsing the entire JSON payload. There's no `resultCount` or `resultBytes` summary field. Compare to the write side which logs `result` as a single `int` TAPIStatus — that side is fine. The read side over-shares: the LLM client got the data, the log file doesn't need to re-store the entire payload to be debuggable.
recommendation: In `WireLog.WriteRecord`, when `result` is `IList`/`ICollection`/`IDictionary` or implements `IEnumerable` (and isn't already a small JsonNode), serialize as `{ "kind": "collection", "count": N, "sampleFirst": <first item only> }` instead of the full payload. Add an env var `LACERTE_DEBUG_LOG_FULL_RESULTS=1` that opts in to the current verbose behavior for the rare deep-debugging session. This is the right knob alongside the redact-all toggle (which is a separate gap) — it cuts the per-line size from MB to KB on the common large-read path without losing per-call duration/op/args/count signal. Bonus: makes finding-#2 rotation pressure much rarer for typical operator workflows.
rationale: Today the debug log doubles as a copy of every read payload. That's not observability — that's a full data export. The operator needs counts + samples, not the dataset.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED via direct read of LacerteSessionManager.cs lines 455-617 and WireLog.cs lines 145-462. Every read chokepoint (ListClients, ReadClient, ReadTable, ReadSubclients, ReadStates, ReadStatuses, ReadForms, ReadDetail, ReadEFStatus) wraps its body in WireLog.Record<T>(...) where T is IReadOnlyList<IReadOnlyDictionary<string,object?>>. WriteRecord at WireLog.cs:398-462 builds a dictionary with record["result"] = result and feeds the full payload to JsonSerializer.Serialize before passing it to Redact. There is no count/sample summarization, no size cap, and no opt-in switch — every read is mirrored to disk in full. For ListClients(limit=int.MaxValue-equivalent) or ReadTable(1) on a 5k-row DBF this produces multi-MB log lines per call.

NOT a Phase-14 duplicate. Phase 14 WireLog tasks were: P14-012 (file-handle reuse — orthogonal), P14-018/P14-019/P14-057 (redaction expansion + JsonNode walker — those harden WHAT is redacted, not how much is logged), P14-067 (drop dead ResetForTests). None of the 71 landed fixes address result-payload volume or add count/sample summarization. P14-013 caps the idempotency cache and P14-014 caps the SQL fetch — neither caps log-line size.

Fully actionable off-Windows: the entire change lives in WireLog.WriteRecord plus a unit test. No bridge, no COM, no Lacerte install. The existing WireLog tests demonstrate the test seam (EnableForTests / FlushForTests / Redact) already used by Phase-14 redaction tests.

IsUseful: yes. The sim store currently seeds modest fixtures but ReadTable is the same chokepoint live-mode ODBC reads will hit on real-world client rosters (the project's spec assumes thousands of clients per practice). Operators with LACERTE_DEBUG_WIRE=1 enabled for a few hours would see logs grow from KB to GB. The summary line {kind, count, sampleFirst} keeps every operationally useful signal (op, duration, count, shape).

Minor refinement to recommendation: the JsonNode walker added in P14-057 is the right place to plug this in — summarize JsonArray nodes assigned to the "result" key when length > N, rather than introducing a separate IEnumerable type-sniff path. This stays consistent with the post-P14-057 architecture (one structured walker, regex only as fallback). Also: the proposed env var should be named consistently with the existing LACERTE_DEBUG_* family.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: In WireLog.WriteRecord, after JsonSerializer.Serialize but BEFORE Redact, post-process the parsed JsonNode to summarize large arrays under the top-level \"result\" key. Concretely: parse the serialized record back into a JsonNode (or build the record as a JsonObject from the start to skip the round-trip), and if the result value is a JsonArray with Count > LACERTE_DEBUG_LOG_RESULT_SAMPLE (default 5), replace it with {\"kind\":\"collection\",\"count\":N,\"sample\":[first 1-5 items]}. Apply the same summarization recursively if any sampled item is itself a large array (depth cap = 2 to keep it bounded). Gate the summarization behind an opt-out env var LACERTE_DEBUG_LOG_FULL_RESULTS=1 (default: summarize) so deep-debugging sessions can still capture the full payload. Land three xUnit cases in WireLogTests: (1) sub-threshold result (e.g. 3 rows) logs as-is; (2) above-threshold result (e.g. 5000 fake DbfRow dicts) logs as a {kind,count,sample} object with sample.Length == 5 and count == 5000; (3) LACERTE_DEBUG_LOG_FULL_RESULTS=1 disables summarization. Keep the existing redaction pipeline downstream of the summarization so sampled rows still pass through RedactNode + ScrubFieldValuePairs (the sampled rows are real DbfRow dicts and can carry SSN/EmailID/etc.). Add a one-line entry to the WireLog DECISIONS.md block landed in P14-037 explaining the summarization policy. No Bridge/ODBC/Windows dependency — entire change is in WireLog.cs plus tests.

title: Idempotency cache: type-mismatch on cached Result misreports as 'different payload fingerprint'
description: In TryReplayIdempotent (lines 1349-1359): when the cached entry's PayloadFingerprint matches the new payload, the code tries `entry.Result is T match`. If the cast fails (e.g., somehow a CreateClientResult was cached under a key now being used by WriteField returning int), the code falls through to throw IdempotencyConflict with reason = 'Idempotency key reused with a different payload fingerprint.' That message is FACTUALLY wrong in this branch — the fingerprint matched. This case can arise via developer error (operator reuses a key across tools) or via a future refactor that changes return types; the misleading error sends the diagnostician chasing a payload-canonicalization bug that isn't there. The actual cause (key reused across operations) is invisible.
recommendation: Split the throw into two branches: (a) when `entry.PayloadFingerprint != payload` → throw with reason 'Idempotency key reused with a different payload fingerprint.' (the existing message). (b) when fingerprint matches but cached type != T → throw with reason 'Idempotency key reused across operations with different return types (cached: <cachedType>, requested: <T>).' Include both in the context dict so the operator can see exactly which keys collide. Add one test that primes the cache with an int result, then calls WriteDetail (also int) and CreateClient (CreateClientResult) under the same key to demonstrate the disambiguation.
rationale: Phase-14 P14-005 closed the TOCTOU race but left the error-message branch wrong for the secondary failure mode. Trivial fix, real DX win when (not if) the case fires.

verdict.reasoning: Verified in LacerteSessionManager.cs lines 1349-1359: when entry.PayloadFingerprint == payload but `entry.Result is T match` fails, control falls through to the same `throw new LacerteSDKError(...IdempotencyConflict, { reason = "Idempotency key reused with a different payload fingerprint." })`. The reason string is factually wrong on that branch — the fingerprint matched; the failure was a return-type mismatch. The inline comment at line 1352 ("Cached result type mismatch — treat as conflict.") even acknowledges this branch but reuses the wrong message. Phase-14 covered TOCTOU (P14-005), TTL/eviction (P14-013/P14-064), timing-safe compare (P14-064), and BuildPayload short-circuit (P14-042) but did NOT touch the error-shape disambiguation. Off-Windows actionable — pure C# change with a SimulationStore-backed unit test using existing WriteField (int) vs CreateClient (CreateClientResult) tools. Low severity (only fires on operator key reuse across tools or a future return-type refactor) but real DX win that prevents diagnostician misdirection.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: In TryReplayIdempotent (LacerteSessionManager.cs ~1349-1359), split the conflict throw into two distinct branches so the error message matches the actual failure mode: (1) `entry.PayloadFingerprint != payload` → keep existing reason "Idempotency key reused with a different payload fingerprint." and include the cached + requested fingerprint prefixes (first 8 chars only — full base64 is noise) in the context dict. (2) Fingerprint matches but `entry.Result is T` fails → throw with reason "Idempotency key reused across operations with different return types." and include `cachedType = entry.Result?.GetType().FullName ?? "null"` and `requestedType = typeof(T).FullName` in the context dict (serialize as strings, not Type objects — Type does not round-trip through System.Text.Json). Keep the synthetic status code as IdempotencyConflict (9102) for both — no new status code needed. Add one Xunit fact in IdempotencyTests (or LacerteSessionManagerTests, wherever the P14-005 stress test landed) that: (a) calls WriteField with key "K1" (returns int), (b) calls CreateClient with same key "K1" (returns CreateClientResult), (c) asserts the second call throws LacerteSDKError with code 9102, reason containing "different return types", and context dict containing both type names. This is off-Windows-actionable via SimulationStore. ~15 LOC change + ~25 LOC test.

title: TaxYear floor enforced as 2018 but TY18 is documented support boundary — fence-post is silent
description: Spec §1: 'Lacerte TY18+ installed'. Spec §5 status code 25 InValidTaxYear remediation says 'Set LACERTE_DEFAULT_TAX_YEAR >= 2018'. The code in SetContext + SimulateCreateClient + SimulateFieldWrite uses `year < 2018` as the floor — TY2018 is accepted. But the spec also names TY21 as the schema-shift boundary and TY24 (or current year) as the upper edge of installed coverage. Three subtle holes: (1) No upper-bound check — a typo passing `year = 2098` is silently accepted and then misroutes to `GetOrAddModule` which creates a phantom in-memory cell. (2) `CanUseNewApis` returns `year >= 2021` unconditionally in sim, but a year >= 2026 still routes through that path even though no Lacerte module exists for it. (3) The Modules catalog has no per-module 'first supported year' field — e.g. Benefit (5500) shipped on a different timeline than Individual — so a 2018 Benefit context is accepted in sim and the operator only learns at live runtime that the module-year cell doesn't exist. Off-by-floor only, but worth flagging because it lights up as confusing live errors.
recommendation: Add an upper-bound sanity check: reject taxYear > (current calendar year + 1) with a clear synthetic 'TaxYearTooNew' error, since the SDK never has data for a year not yet released. Optionally extend ModuleInfo with `int FirstSupportedYear` (default 2018 for I/C/P/S, later for the specialized modules per spec's TY18 footnote) and validate per-module in SetContext. Either fix is sim-actionable; the spec-tightening is a half-day's work that closes a class of confusing live errors.
rationale: Round 1 found year-related issues (P14-009 covers ARCHITECTURE.md tax-year boundaries; P14-020 hoisted module catalog) but no finding addressed the upper-bound + per-module-floor combination. The audit task explicitly asked for 'TY18 vs TY21 vs TY24 boundaries: are off-by-one year boundaries correct in CanUseNewApis?' which this surfaces.

verdict.reasoning:
Verified by direct file inspection. LacerteSessionManager.SetContext (line 378) and SimulateCreateClient inline check (line 907) both gate only on `year < 2018` with no upper bound. SyntheticStatusCodes.cs has TaxYearTooOld (9003) but no TaxYearTooNew counterpart. Meanwhile ConnectionStringBuilder.cs:77 ALREADY validates `taxYear > 2099` — but throws a raw `ArgumentException`, not a structured `LacerteSDKError`, so the two enforcement points are inconsistent: SetContext accepts year=2098, then a downstream Odbc.Query call would throw an unstructured ArgumentException that bypasses the LacerteSDKError envelope contract. This is a real fence-post + error-shape consistency gap.

Phase-14 duplicate scan: P14-009 (CI workflow — NOT year-boundary docs as the finding's rationale incorrectly claims), P14-020 (module catalog hoist), P14-032 (overlay per-year semantics) all touched adjacent areas but none added an upper-bound year gate, a TaxYearTooNew synthetic code, or per-module FirstSupportedYear. No Phase-14 task surfaces year-ceiling enforcement.

Caveats that tighten the recommendation: (a) the finding's "phantom in-memory cell" claim is weak — SetContext already validates module membership, so misrouting is bounded. (b) The CanUseNewApis claim (year >= 2026 routes through UpdateTaxReturn path "even though no Lacerte module exists") is technically true in sim but harmless since sim is a deterministic decision; live mode delegates to the bridge probe. (c) The per-module FirstSupportedYear half is speculative without spec citations naming which specialized modules (B/N/T/R/F) shipped on which timelines — should be deferred or dropped. The upper-bound gate is the high-value piece worth landing.
